record.file_problem: This is repository metadata, README text, and a file list, not the full paper text. A PDF is listed in the repository but its contents are not provided here.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a reimplementation of the difference-in-means extraction and ablation analysis, with behavioral results on additional model variants and settings.
record.gate_note: Recorded only results stated in the README. The listed figures and JSON files are not independently readable from the file list. Extraction/layer-selection values used as diagnostics without a reported behavioral outcome are not rows.
record.test_reason: Reimplements the original difference-in-means extraction, ablation and addition pipeline on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B. It reports refusal rates under ablation (V1), under cross-model transplant (V6, V8) and under phase-gated ablation in a reasoning model (V8). The verdict rests on the README only; the listed PDF was not available.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Extraction position decides whether the Instruct direction is causal (L1 user_end: weak; L19 last_full: removes refusal). R1-Distill's L22 direction acts only inside the think phase. The Instruct-to-R1 transplant induces refusal but not selectively (safe prompts too), beyond an L1 negative control. Ablation also raises jailbreak ASR. Source is the README only; the PDF was unread.
record.recipe_differences: Reimplementation of the difference-in-means extraction and ablation pipeline, with explicit choices for extraction position, layer selection, and intervention form; also reports transplant and phase-aware analyses. Repository type: replication/reimplementation.
record.method_sensitivity: Extraction position changes the Instruct ablation outcome substantially: user_end at L1 has a small effect, while last_full at L19 removes refusal. Phase also changes the R1-Distill ablation outcome: think-only matches full-rollout ablation; answer-only matches baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating Instruct's L19 direction raises JailbreakBench ASR from 24% to 33% (JBC) and 50% to 69.5% (PAIR).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction ablation compounds with prompt-based jailbreaks, raising attack success.

record.problems: This record is based only on the README and file list, not the listed paper PDF. The README does not report uncertainty estimates. The phase-aware result is qualitative and does not provide the label names or category rates. The reported WikiText-2 perplexity check concerns a transplant, not a broad test of abilities after ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were included from the listed JSON, figure, or PDF files because their contents are not provided in the repository text; README results were all recorded.

untested.parts: Capability retention after ablation (ablation perplexity files exist but no numbers are in the README); addition on Instruct itself.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, and whether training against ablation adds robustness. Neither is tested.
No multi-direction, cone or affine comparison.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal.
No cross-language transfer; no base-to-instruct transfer results in the README.
The base, instruct and distilled variants are compared, but no result on training dependence is reported in the README.

missing.what: Refusal rates for full-rollout L22 ablation on R1-Distill, and the four phase-aware category rates
Perplexity under ablation for Instruct L19 and R1-Distill L22
Cross-model cosine similarity of directions (base, instruct, R1-Distill) against a basis-drift null
Base-model extraction and ablation results; transplant at other α and layer cells

record.verdict_notes: Unreviewed course-project repository; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The reader's V6 limits_scope label for non-selectivity is dropped: V1 itself predicts refusal induced on harmless prompts. Instead, limits_scope is given for incomplete induction. V3 is relabeled untested.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report a broad evaluation of other abilities after refusal-direction ablation, or additive steering on Instruct itself.
No released-model weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No result is reported for training against the ablation.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The reported transplant is from Instruct to R1-Distill only; the README does not establish transfer across languages or other model pairs.
Although the repository includes differently trained model variants, the README does not report a result testing whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
The reasoning-model evidence is for R1-Distill and the described L22 phase-aware ablation; no wider set of reasoning models is reported.
